issues.body:
The new reject is placed in maybeDecompressBytes, which is shared by BOTH entry points: maybeDecompressFile (web file upload) and fetchRdfDocument (the URL tab). The URL tab is persona-independent — import-drawer.tsx:496 renders `{tab === "url" && <UrlPane .../>}` with no `native` guard, and onImportUrl (import-drawer.tsx:353-357) calls fetchRdfDocument(target) unconditionally; only the FILE tab branches on `native` (lines 470/479).

Consequence: in the Tauri desktop shell, importing https://host/data.nt.bz2 now throws 'Bzip2 archives are supported only by the desktop app.' — a message that is false in the context it is shown. It is also a capability regression: on main this path reached decompressDatasetBytes, whose 'bzip2' codec decodes via seek-bzip (packages/sparq-client/src/decompress.ts decodeBzip2), and both seek-bzip and buffer are still declared dependencies. The desktop FILE tab is unaffected (native loader), so the loss is confined to desktop URL imports — but it is real, and the wrong-persona wording contradicts the PR's own honesty goal.

If the underlying motivation is that in-browser bzip2 does not actually work, the same argument applies to the Tauri webview, and the message must then say so plainly rather than pointing at the desktop app.
issues.fix_hint: Make the gate persona-aware instead of unconditional. Either (a) give maybeDecompressBytes an options arg (e.g. `{ allowBzip2 }` or `{ nativeLoaderAvailable }`) that import-drawer passes from the same `native` flag it already uses at lines 470/479, rejecting only on web; or (b) keep the reject global but route the desktop URL fetch through the native loader for bzip2. Either way the thrown text must be true where it is displayed — e.g. 'Bzip2 archives cannot be decoded in the browser; use the desktop app.' on web, and no reject at all (or a different message) when running under Tauri. Add a unit test in file-decompress.test.ts that pins BOTH branches: bzip2 rejected with the allow-flag off, and decompression attempted with it on.
issues.title: bzip2 hard-reject fires on the DESKTOP persona's URL tab, telling a desktop user to use the desktop app

issues.body:
Every other surface got a bzip2 caveat this round (WebFilePane text, drop hint, dialog Description, status-bar title, engine-context doc, README). UrlPane (import-drawer.tsx:973-999) was missed: it still says 'Fetch an RDF document, including a compressed archive, from a URL', with no indication that bzip2 is excluded.

Worse, the FormatNote rendered just below passes `compressed={isCompressed(url)}`, and rdf-format.ts's COMPRESSION_EXTS still contains 'bz2'. So typing a .bz2 URL shows an affirmative 'compressed' affordance, and then the import hard-fails with the desktop-only error. That is the same silently-misleading pattern the file tab was cleaned up to remove.
issues.fix_hint: Update the UrlPane paragraph to match the WebFilePane wording (gzip/zip/zstd decoded in-tab; bzip2 and HDT desktop-only), and stop presenting .bz2/.tbz URLs as supported-compressed on the web persona — either exclude them from the isCompressed()-driven hint on web, or have FormatNote render an explicit 'bzip2 requires the desktop app' warning instead of the neutral compressed badge.
issues.title: URL-tab copy and the compressed hint were not narrowed alongside the file-tab copy

issues.body:
The test is titled '.zst upload is decoded before RDF format detection', but it cannot discriminate the format-detection half. guessFormat() calls stripCompression(), whose COMPRESSION_EXTS (gui/app/src/lib/rdf-format.ts:28) already contains 'zst' — so guessFormat('browser-upload.nt.zst') and guessFormat('browser-upload.nt') both return 'ntriples'. Reverting import-drawer.tsx:270 to guessFormat(file.name) leaves this test green. The payload is also N-Triples, which is a valid Turtle subset, so even a wrong 'turtle' guess would parse and the SELECT would still match.

The test is genuinely non-vacuous for what actually matters here — the zstd decode (undecompressed frame bytes would decode to mojibake and the ok banner would never appear) — so this is not a blocker. But round 3's recorded nit stands: no test goes red if the effectiveName plumbing regresses.
issues.fix_hint: Use a member whose format is NOT reachable from the outer name and NOT Turtle-compatible: a STORED zip named bundle.zip whose single member is payload.nq containing a quad in a named graph (reuse the storedZip helper shape from file-decompress.test.ts). guessFormat('bundle.zip') is 'turtle' (zip is not in COMPRESSION_EXTS), Turtle rejects the 4th term, and asserting the quad lands with its graph preserved goes red the moment line 270 regresses. Rename the current test to say what it pins — e.g. '.zst upload is decompressed before parsing'.
issues.title: The new e2e cannot fail on the effectiveName wiring it is named after (round-3 nit still open)

issues.body: The comment above WEB_RDF_ACCEPT now states 'Tar containers (.tgz/.tbz) are unsupported because decompression yields TAR rather than RDF'. Only .tbz is actually enforced (it is in the new bzip2 suffix list). .tgz is merely dropped from WEB_RDF_ACCEPT, which is only a file-picker filter: WebFilePane's handleDrop (import-drawer.tsx:684-714) passes every dropped File straight to readFilesWithDecompress with no accept check, and a user can pick 'All files' in the dialog. Such a .tgz still matches CODEC_EXTENSIONS.gzip in @sparq/client, gunzips to TAR bytes, and reaches the RDF parser as binary garbage with a confusing parse error — where .tbz gets an explicit (if wrongly-worded) message. Pre-existing behaviour, but the new comment now overstates it.
issues.fix_hint: Either reject .tgz/.tar.gz explicitly next to the bzip2 check in maybeDecompressBytes with an honest message ('tar archives are not supported — upload the RDF file directly'), or soften the comment to say .tgz is merely excluded from the picker filter rather than unsupported.
issues.title: The new .tgz comment claims tar containers are unsupported, but nothing rejects them

verdict.summary:
Round 4 adds a .zst e2e; I verified the fixture is spec-valid (descriptor 0x20 => single-segment, FCS at byte 5, raw last block (len<<3)|1) and that it is non-vacuous for the decode path: without decompression the frame decodes to mojibake and the import banner would be 'error'. The round-3 zip unit test and the doc narrowing also still hold up.

However, tracing the bzip2 gate through the whole drawer surfaces a defect neither round 2 nor round 3 caught: the reject lives in the SHARED maybeDecompressBytes, and the URL tab is rendered on BOTH personas (import-drawer.tsx:496 has no `native` guard) with onImportUrl calling fetchRdfDocument unconditionally (line 355). So inside the Tauri desktop app, importing a .bz2 URL now fails with 'Bzip2 archives are supported only by the desktop app.' — self-contradictory, and a capability loss versus main, where decompressDatasetBytes decoded bzip2 via seek-bzip in the webview. That is exactly the honesty class this PR set out to fix, so I am blocking on it.

Secondary: the URL surface was not narrowed with the rest of the copy (UrlPane still says 'including a compressed archive'; FormatNote's isCompressed() still counts .bz2, so a .bz2 URL renders a 'compressed' affordance and then hard-fails).

On progress: I am reporting 'regressing' per the literal scale (a new finding at a higher severity than round 3's single nit), but in fairness the major is NOT newly introduced by round 4 — the gate landed in round 3 and was missed then. The code did not get worse this round; the review got deeper. Round 3's nit also still stands: guessFormat already strips .zst (rdf-format.ts COMPRESSION_EXTS), so the new e2e's format assertion cannot go red if import-drawer.tsx:270 reverts to file.name.
